qa_pairs.question: What is the primary purpose of the Metrix portal for Alliance users?
qa_pairs.answer: The Metrix portal is a website for Alliance users to track their resource usage (CPUs, GPUs, memory, filesystems) in real time by collecting information on compute nodes and management servers.

qa_pairs.question: Which Alliance clusters are accessible through the Metrix portal?
qa_pairs.answer: The Metrix portal provides access for Rorqual, Narval, and Nibi clusters.

qa_pairs.question: What types of general information can users find under the main tabs of the Metrix portal?
qa_pairs.answer: Users can find graphs for filesystem performance, usage statistics for login nodes, cluster scheduler statistics, frequently used scientific software, and bandwidth statistics for data transfer nodes.

qa_pairs.question: What specific details are available to users under the "User portal" tab in Metrix?
qa_pairs.answer: The "User portal" tab displays filesystem quotas and the user's 10 most recent jobs, with options to view job details or all jobs under the "Job statistics" tab.

qa_pairs.question: What information does the "Job statistics" tab provide to Alliance users?
qa_pairs.answer: The "Job statistics" tab shows current usage (CPU cores, memory, GPUs), historical usage graphs, filesystem activity (IOPS, bandwidth), and a list of all jobs with filtering and search options.

qa_pairs.question: When viewing a specific CPU job on the Metrix portal, what details can users access regarding its execution?
qa_pairs.answer: Users can view the job name, number, username, status, submission script (if not interactive), submission command, scheduler information, and compare allocated versus used resources.

qa_pairs.question: What types of performance graphs are available for individual CPU jobs on the Metrix portal?
qa_pairs.answer: Performance graphs for individual CPU jobs include CPU core usage over time, memory usage, processes and threads, filesystem usage (IOPS, data transfer rate), node resources (bandwidth), local disk usage (IOPS, bandwidth, space), and power consumption.

qa_pairs.question: What is the main difference when viewing a CPU job that is part of a job array compared to a regular CPU job on the Metrix portal?
qa_pairs.answer: The page for a CPU job in an array is similar to a regular CPU job, but it includes an "Other jobs in the array" section listing related job numbers, their status, name, and start/finish times.

qa_pairs.question: What unique performance metrics are displayed for GPU jobs on the Metrix portal that are not typically found for CPU jobs?
qa_pairs.answer: GPU job metrics include Streaming Multiprocessors (SM) setting, SM occupancy, Tensor setting, FP64/FP32/FP16 floating-point operations, GPU memory usage, GPU memory access cycles, GPU power consumption, and GPU bandwidth on the PCIe bus.

qa_pairs.question: What is the purpose of the "Account statistics" section within the Metrix portal?
qa_pairs.answer: The "Account statistics" section allows users to view their group's usage for both CPU and GPU resources, broken down into two subsections.

qa_pairs.question: What specific usage details can be found under the "CPU accounts" section of the Metrix portal?
qa_pairs.answer: The "CPU accounts" section shows the total CPU cores requested by the group, usage over months, priority status, most frequently used applications, resources used by each user, wasted CPU cores, wasted memory, filesystem activity, and the group's last jobs.

qa_pairs.question: What information is available under the "GPU accounts" section in the Metrix portal?
qa_pairs.answer: The "GPU accounts" section displays total GPU requests for the group, usage over months, priority status, frequently used software, resources used by each user (GPUs, CPUs, memory), wasted GPUs/CPUs/memory, filesystem activity, and the group's last jobs.

qa_pairs.question: What kind of information is presented in the "Cloud statistics" section of the Metrix portal?
qa_pairs.answer: The "Cloud statistics" section displays a table of all virtual machines associated with an account, including their type (Flavor) and unique identifier (UUID), along with individual usage statistics for each virtual machine (CPU cores, memory, disk bandwidth, IOPS, and network bandwidth).

qa_pairs.question: How can users compare requested versus actual resource usage for their jobs on the Metrix portal?
qa_pairs.answer: In the "Ressources" section for both CPU and GPU jobs, users can compare the "Allocated" and "Used" columns for various parameters to see the resources consumed by their job.

qa_pairs.question: How can the Metrix portal help users identify filesystem activity for their jobs?
qa_pairs.answer: For individual jobs, graphs show the number of I/O operations per second (IOPS) and the data transfer rate (bandwidth) between the job and the filesystem over time, helping to identify periods of high or low activity.
